strengths: Identifies an important, practical, and previously overlooked failure mode in LLM unlearning: standard unlearning objectives severely impair 'contextual utility', rendering models unable to utilize or reason over unlearned facts even when legitimately provided in context (e.g., in RAG or user-supplied prompts).
The proposed plug-in objective (regularizing the model's contextual predictive distribution against the pre-unlearning model via KL divergence) is elegant, intuitive, and model/method-agnostic.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple unlearning frameworks (RMU, NPO, UNDIAL, DPO, GradDiff, PDU, SimNPO), multiple architectures (Gemma-2B-IT, Qwen-8B), and multiple benchmarks (TOFU and PISTOL).

Extensive robustness and stress testing under diverse context conditions, including paraphrased contexts, reasoning-based contexts, long noisy passages, and multi-distractor conflicting evidence settings.
Careful validation of evaluation methodology, including human correlation analysis for the Claude-based LLM-Judge metric (Cohen's kappa of ~0.95).
weaknesses: The method assumes access to structured or synthesized contextual examples ($S_f^{ctx}$) during unlearning. In practical settings where the forget request consists of raw documents or arbitrary factual statements, generating suitable (context, question, answer) pairs requires an additional generation/templating pipeline whose sensitivity is not deeply explored.

The trade-off between contextual utility and absolute unlearning compliance is not thoroughly discussed in safety-critical contexts (e.g., hazardous CBRN knowledge as in WMDP), where one might intentionally prefer the model to refuse even when given context, versus benign privacy/copyright settings where contextual utility is desired.

As acknowledged in the limitations and visible in the experimental tables, preserving contextual utility can occasionally introduce a slight regression in Direct QA forgetting (e.g., small increases in Direct QA LLM-Judge scores), reflecting an inherent tension between forgetting representations and conditioning on them.

strengths: Identifies an important, practical, and previously overlooked failure mode in machine unlearning: while standard unlearning objectives successfully erase target facts from parametric memory, they often catastrophically degrade the model's ability to utilize those same facts when provided in-context (e.g., via RAG or user prompts).

Comprehensive empirical investigation evaluating six distinct unlearning algorithms (including RMU, NPO, and UNDIAL) across two model architectures (Gemma-2B-IT and Qwen3-8B), clearly demonstrating the ubiquity of contextual suppression across methods.

The proposed context-aware regularization objective is intuitive, modular, and easily integrated into existing unlearning pipelines without altering the core unlearning mechanism or requiring external ground-truth supervision.

Thorough evaluation and robustness analyses, including human-agreement validation for the LLM judge, varying forget set proportions (1%, 5%, 10%), evaluation on structurally entangled data (PISTOL), and evaluations under noisy contexts, reasoning queries, and multiple conflicting distractors.
weaknesses: Constructing the contextual unlearning set $S_{ctx}^f$ requires pairing forget-set examples with suitable context templates during unlearning. In real-world unstructured unlearning scenarios (e.g., broad copyright removals or unstructured text redaction), generating or formatting appropriate $(q, c)$ pairs may require non-trivial data curation.

The objective aligns the contextual predictive distribution directly with the pre-unlearned model using KL divergence on specific prompt formats. The manuscript would benefit from evaluating cross-format generalization where the inference prompt structure differs significantly from the context template used during unlearning.

There is a minor but noticeable trade-off with parametric forgetting: in several settings (e.g., Table 2 for Gemma-2B-IT RMU and NPO, and Table 7 for PISTOL), the context-aware variant shows slight increases in Direct QA recall, suggesting a subtle risk of retaining parametric associations when anchoring to the original model.

strengths: Novel and practically significant problem setup: While LLM unlearning research predominantly focuses on erasing parametric knowledge (Direct QA) and preserving unrelated capabilities (retain set utility), this work identifies an important and previously overlooked failure mode—the degradation of 'contextual utility' (the ability of an unlearned model to accurately utilize the unlearned knowledge when it is legitimately reintroduced in the prompt, such as in RAG or document QA).

Comprehensive empirical evidence of contextual collapse: The paper systematically evaluates six popular unlearning algorithms (RMU, NPO, UNDIAL, GradDiff, GradAscent, DPO) on Gemma-2B-IT and Qwen3-8B, conclusively showing that state-of-the-art methods severely impair contextual grounding—in some cases like RMU, reducing Contextual QA accuracy almost to zero.

Simple, modular, and effective remedy: The proposed context-aware unlearning objective introduces a KL-divergence term aligning contextual predictions with the frozen reference model. It is easy to plug into existing unlearning frameworks, incurs low overhead via offline caching, and consistently restores contextual performance without noticeably sacrificing forgetting efficacy or retain-set utility.

Thorough evaluation and robustness analyses: The submission provides extensive experiments across multiple forget ratios (1%, 5%, 10%), two distinct benchmarks (TOFU and PISTOL), human validation for LLM-Judge evaluations (Cohen's kappa > 0.94), and stress tests under context variations (paraphrasing, reasoning prompts, noisy GPT-generated paragraphs, and multiple conflicting distractors).
weaknesses: Assumption of paired contextual data: The proposed objective requires access to paired context-question-answer tuples $(q, c, a) \in S_f^{ctx}$ during the unlearning stage. In certain real-world unlearning scenarios (e.g., unlearning arbitrary documents or raw text spans), cleanly paired contextual question-answering examples may not be readily available without additional synthetic data generation.

Reliance on synthetic/fictitious benchmarks: Experiments are primarily conducted on TOFU (fictitious author profiles) and PISTOL (relational data). Evaluating on more natural unlearning datasets containing real copyrighted texts or actual PII extraction attacks would strengthen the empirical claims.

Lack of mechanistic interpretability: While Section A.5 provides intuitive qualitative explanations for why parametric penalties suppress contextual grounding, the paper does not empirically investigate model internals (e.g., via attention visualization, probing, or activation patching) to explain mechanistically how standard unlearning disrupts in-context grounding and how the KL term repairs it.

strengths: The paper identifies a timely, practically important, and under-explored failure mode of machine unlearning: while existing unlearning methods suppress internal factual recall (Direct QA), they severely impair the model's ability to use the unlearned facts even when explicitly supplied as context in the prompt (Contextual QA).

The proposed context-aware unlearning objective is conceptually clean, modular, and easy to plug into existing unlearning frameworks (such as RMU, NPO, and UNDIAL) via an auxiliary KL divergence constraint on contextual queries.

Empirical improvements are substantial and consistent across two model families (Gemma-2B-IT and Qwen3-8B). In particular, methods that suffered catastrophic collapse in contextual grounding (e.g., RMU dropping to near 0.0 LLM-Judge) are restored to near-perfect performance (~0.97–0.99) without sacrificing Direct QA forgetting or general retain utility.
The paper is clearly structured and well-written, with thorough ablations over forget set sizes (1%, 5%, 10%) and regularizer weights, along with illuminating qualitative case studies.
weaknesses: The experimental evaluation is restricted entirely to the synthetic TOFU benchmark (fictitious author profiles). Evaluating on more diverse or real-world unlearning benchmarks (such as WMDP for hazardous knowledge, MUSE, or real copyright/PII datasets) would significantly strengthen the empirical support and verify whether this contextual collapse and its fix generalize.

The construction of the contextual forget set $S_f^{ctx}$ assumes access to explicit context-question pairs $(q, c)$. While straightforward in TOFU, in many real-world unlearning scenarios the forget set consists of unstructured text or documents. The manuscript lacks discussion on how $S_f^{ctx}$ can be systematically constructed or synthesized in realistic unlearning pipelines.

Section 6.2 evaluates robustness to context variants (paraphrased and reasoning contexts) on only a single qualitative case study rather than providing systematic quantitative metrics across the evaluation split.

strengths: Identifies an important, practical, and largely overlooked failure mode in machine unlearning: standard unlearning methods often impair an LLM's ability to utilize forgotten knowledge even when that knowledge is explicitly provided in context (e.g., in RAG or user prompts).

Provides a comprehensive empirical diagnostic across six representative unlearning algorithms (RMU, NPO, UNDIAL, DPO, GradAscent, GradDiff) and two modern instruction-tuned LLMs (Gemma-2B-IT and Qwen3-8B), revealing severe degradation in contextual QA across forget ratios.

Proposes a simple, modular, and plug-in objective based on KL consistency between the unlearned model and the original model on contextual queries, demonstrating large gains in contextual QA with minimal impact on forgetting effectiveness and retain utility.
The paper is clearly structured, well-written, and easy to follow, with intuitive motivating figures and illustrative qualitative case studies.
weaknesses: Empirical evaluation is restricted to a single benchmark (TOFU). While TOFU is a standard benchmark for unlearning synthetic author profiles, evaluating on other unlearning benchmarks (such as MUSE or real-world factual unlearning tasks) would substantiate whether this issue and fix generalize across domains.

Robustness to contextual distribution shifts is only demonstrated via a single qualitative case study (Table 4). In real-world retrieval-augmented settings, retrieved contexts vary substantially in phrasing, length, and distractor content compared to the training prompt template. A systematic, quantitative evaluation across the full forget set under noisy, paraphrased, and distractor-laden contexts is missing.

Missing a key ablation/baseline regarding the context set: The proposed method constructs contextual queries using the forget set $S_f^{ctx}$. It remains unclear whether this context regularization strictly requires $S_f^{ctx}$, or whether preserving general in-context grounding could be achieved by applying the contextual KL term on retain set context ($S_r^{ctx}$) or generic QA/reading comprehension data.

strengths: Identifies an important and previously overlooked vulnerability in LLM unlearning: standard unlearning algorithms often suppress 'contextual utility', causing models to fail at reading comprehension and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) when forgotten facts are explicitly provided in-context.

Comprehensive empirical diagnosis across six unlearning methods (RMU, NPO, UNDIAL, DPO, GradAscent, GradDiff) on two distinct open-weight models (Gemma-2B-IT and Qwen3-8B), revealing significant contextual degradation across multiple forget ratios.
The proposed context-aware regularization is conceptually straightforward, modular, and can be integrated into diverse unlearning loss formulations with minimal implementation overhead.

The empirical results on the TOFU benchmark show that the method successfully restores contextual QA accuracy (bringing LLM-judge scores from near-zero in RMU and ~0.5-0.8 in others to >0.95) without substantially harming direct QA forgetting or retain utility.
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted entirely to the synthetic TOFU benchmark; the manuscript lacks validation on real-world unlearning domains such as WMDP (hazardous knowledge removal), MUSE, or PII/copyright datasets.

Potential circularity in the training/evaluation setup: the context-regularization term trains directly on the contextualized forget examples $S_f^{ctx} = (q, c, a)$ using the same template/format evaluated at test time. Beyond a qualitative single-sample case study in Section 6.2, there is no systematic quantitative evaluation on out-of-distribution or paraphrased contexts, multi-document distractors, or unseen queries over the provided context.

The mathematical formulation of the contextual consistency objective in Section 4.2 is underspecified: $KL(p_w(\cdot | q, c) \parallel p_{\text{orig}}(\cdot | q, c))$ does not make clear whether the KL divergence is computed over the full sequence space, teacher-forced over reference tokens $a$, or sampled autoregressively, nor does it specify the exact token masking applied during optimization.

The paper does not adequately disambiguate whether vanilla unlearning induces entity/token-specific contextual suppression or general degradation of in-context learning/reading comprehension abilities. Testing general RAG benchmarks (e.g., SQuAD, MS-MARCO) on non-forget topics is necessary to characterize the scope of the impairment.

The convergence criterion and hyperparameter selection ($\lambda_c$) described in Appendix A.4 rely on joint monitoring of test-set Contextual QA, Direct QA, and Model Utility, which risks overfitting to the evaluation split.
